title: User-consent-aware canary with feature gates and revert playbook
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Certain customers require privacy-preserving rollouts where requests from users who have not consented to behavioral experimentation must never be routed to canary variants. This PR introduces a consent-aware canary path, explicit feature-gates for experiment eligibility, and an automated revert playbook that triggers on either privacy policy violations or SLO/regression signals. Design: add a ConsentRouter component that evaluates signed consent tokens and user-level flags; extend RolloutPolicy to include consent_gate (opt-in/opt-out/strict) and per-cohort mapping; implement a RevertOrchestrator that listens to telemetry gates (latency/error/quality and privacy_audit signals) and performs snapshot revert, traffic-quarantine, and safe-drain sequences; surface new toggles in Console for admins to preview impacted cohorts. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is off and existing rollouts continue to work; if consent_gate omitted, rollout falls back to legacy routing. Tests and validation: unit tests for router and orchestration logic, integration e2e scenarios simulating mixed-consent cohorts, and a staged canary smoke run in perf-canary lab. Rollout plan: land behind a feature flag, enable in staging with synthetic traffic, then enable for a single low-risk customer cohort, monitor key metrics for 48 hours, then widen. Checklist: [x] router implementation [x] controller integration [x] metrics and audit events [x] runbook + console UI [x] e2e smoke tests [x] Linear ticket tags. Notes: this PR intentionally keeps consent evaluation synchronous at the routing layer to avoid accidental shadowing; future work will explore async pre-filtering cache for latency optimization.
